ogch.techniqueProtocols.tappDefinition.title: Technique-Aligned Protocol Profile (TAPP) Definition v3
ogch.techniqueProtocols.tappDefinition.description: A registered Technique-Aligned Protocol Profile (TAPP) definition modeled as a cdi:Activity and schema:Action. The TAPP identity (name, technique, instrument, location) lives at the top level. The standard workflow is encoded in schema:actionProcess as a schema:HowTo containing an ordered sequence of cdi:Activity + schema:Action steps (sample preparation, calibration, acquisition, data processing, quality control). Each workflow step carries its own parameters, reagents, and instruments. TAPP-level parameters that apply across all steps remain at the top level in ada:methodParameters. Integrates Bioschemas vocabulary for computational tools and reagents, DDI-CDI for activity sequence, and dqv:hasQualityMeasurement for quality metrics.

@context.description: JSON-LD context declaring the namespace prefixes used in a method definition. Required for the document to be a valid JSON-LD instance. Bound prefixes must include schema (always), cdi (DDI-CDI), and ada (ADA vocabulary). Additional prefixes (bios, dqv, prov, skos) are recommended when those vocabularies are used in the body of the definition.

@id.description: Persistent URI for this TAPP definition in the registry.

@type.description: Must include cdi:Activity, schema:Action, ada:TAPPDefinition, and bios:LabProtocol.

schema:name.title: Method Name
schema:name.description: Short descriptive name with version (e.g. "JEOL-8530F WDS Major Element Glass v2.1").

schema:identifier.description: DOI or other persistent ID for this method definition.

schema:description.description: Human-readable summary of the method, may be auto-generated from constant parameters at registration time.

schema:datePublished.title: Method Start Date
schema:datePublished.description: ISO 8601 date when this method configuration was first used.

schema:dateModified.description: ISO 8601 date of last update to this definition.

schema:additionalType.description: Further classification of the activity type (e.g. schema:CreateAction for a production method).

schema:measurementTechnique.title: Technique
schema:measurementTechnique.description: The analytical technique this method implements. Must be a DefinedTerm from a controlled vocabulary of techniques.

schema:object.description: Target material(s) this method is designed to analyse (e.g. silicate glass, olivine, spinel). Modeled as DefinedTerm(s) or free text.

schema:instrument.description: Primary instrument specification for this method. Use schema:hasPart for instrument sub-components (spectrometers, detectors).

bios:computationalTool.description: Software tools used for data acquisition, reduction, and processing. Each tool carries name, version, and optional URL.

bios:reagent.description: Reference materials, calibration standards, and chemical reagents used across this method. Reagents specific to a single workflow step should be placed on that step instead.

schema:location.title: Laboratory
schema:location.description: Laboratory where this method was developed. Optional; omit for methods that are instrument-generic.

schema:creator.title: Method Author
schema:creator.description: Person or organisation who defined or is responsible for this method.

schema:actionProcess.description: The standard workflow for this method, expressed as a schema:HowTo containing an ordered sequence of workflow steps. Each step is a cdi:Activity + schema:Action describing a distinct phase (sample preparation, calibration, acquisition, data processing, quality control). Steps carry their own parameters, reagents, instruments, and sub-steps.

ada:methodParameters.description: Method-level parameters that apply across all workflow steps (e.g. method-scoped constants like matrix correction model). Step-specific parameters should be placed on the appropriate workflow step instead.

ada:analyteTemplate.description: Template for per-analyte (element-specific) parameters. Defines the columns that appear in the element table, each with scope, datatype, and constraints. Analyte rows become schema:variableMeasured entries in metadata records. Typically associated with the acquisition workflow step.

ada:analyteColumns.description: Columns of the per-analyte parameter table. Must include exactly one column with schema:valueName "analyte" that identifies the analyzed constituent named in each row.

ada:defaultAnalytes.description: Pre-populated analyte rows for this method. Each entry is an object keyed by analyteColumn names.

dqv:hasQualityMeasurement.description: Quality measurements that characterize the method's expected performance (e.g. analytical precision, accuracy, counting statistics error). Uses the CDIF qualityMeasure building block.

schema:relatedLink.title: Method References
schema:relatedLink.description: Publications, Zenodo records, or other references reports describing or evaluating this method.

WorkflowHowTo.description: The method's standard workflow expressed as a schema:HowTo. Contains an ordered array of workflow steps in schema:step, where each step is a cdi:Activity + schema:Action.

schema:name.description: Name of the workflow (e.g. "EPMA WDS analytical workflow").

schema:url.description: URL to a published protocol document.

schema:step.description: Ordered sequence of workflow steps. Each step is a cdi:Activity + schema:Action describing a distinct phase of the analytical procedure. Must include exactly one sample-preparation step (schema:name "Sample preparation" with schema:additionalType containing "bios:LabProcess"); its schema:position is left to the protocol author.

contains.description: a sample preparation step is required.

WorkflowStep.description: A single step in the analytical workflow, modeled as a cdi:Activity + schema:Action. Each step describes a distinct phase such as sample preparation, instrument calibration, data acquisition, data processing, or quality control. Steps carry their own parameters, instruments, reagents, and may contain sub-steps via schema:actionProcess.

schema:name.description: Name of this workflow step (e.g. "Sample preparation").

schema:description.description: Detailed description of what this step involves.

schema:position.description: Ordinal position in the workflow sequence (1-based).

schema:additionalType.description: Further classification of this step (e.g. bios:LabProcess for wet-lab steps, schema:CreateAction for production steps).

schema:instrument.description: Instrument or equipment used in this step.

bios:computationalTool.description: Software tools used in this step.

bios:reagent.description: Reference materials, standards, or reagents used in this step.

prov:used.description: Input entities consumed or referenced by this step (e.g. prepared sample from a prior step).

schema:result.description: Output entity produced by this step (can be referenced as input by a subsequent step).

schema:object.description: Reference to a prior step whose result is the input for this step (action chaining).

schema:additionalProperty.description: Step-specific parameters (e.g. beam conditions for the acquisition step, matrix correction settings for the data processing step).

schema:actionProcess.description: Sub-workflow for this step, expressed as a nested schema:HowTo with its own ordered steps. Use for steps that have a multi-phase internal procedure (e.g. sample preparation with mount, grind, polish, coat).

dqv:hasQualityMeasurement.description: Quality measurements specific to this workflow step.

MethodParameter.description: A parameter specification for the method, typed as schema:PropertyValueSpecification. Uses schema.org properties for value constraints (defaultValue, minValue, maxValue, readonlyValue, valueRequired) and ada: extensions for analytical method semantics (fieldScope, category, tier). Link to a controlled vocabulary via schema:inDefinedTermSet.

schema:description.description: Guidance text shown to the user in the form.

schema:propertyID.description: URI identifying this parameter type in a formal vocabulary. Links to a skos:Concept or similar term definition.

schema:inDefinedTermSet.description:
Controlled vocabulary providing allowed values for this parameter. When present, form renders a dropdown/select populated from the vocabulary. Four shapes are accepted: (1) a plain URI string identifying an external SKOS ConceptScheme; (2) an object reference ({"@id": "<uri>"}) to a vocabulary defined elsewhere; (3) a LabeledLink (LinkRole with name and URL); (4) an inline schema:DefinedTermSet enumerating the allowed values
    as schema:DefinedTerm objects (replaces the prior ada:enumeration).

anyOf.description: Object reference to a vocabulary defined elsewhere.
Inline schema:DefinedTermSet listing the allowed values as schema:DefinedTerm objects. Use when no external vocabulary URI is available; replaces the deprecated ada:enumeration property.

schema:defaultValue.description: The default value for this parameter. For constant parameters (readonlyValue=true), this is the fixed value. For editable parameters, this is the pre-filled default.

schema:readonlyValue.description: true = constant, fixed for every session (read-only in form). false = editable (default or optional depending on valueRequired).

schema:valueRequired.description: true = must be provided (mandatory). false = optional. Combined with readonlyValue: readonly+required = constant mandatory; !readonly+required = editable mandatory; !readonly+!required = optional.

schema:minValue.description: Minimum allowed numeric value. Defines the lower bound of a valid range at the method level; specific values within this range may be set per element in the analyteTemplate.

schema:maxValue.description: Maximum allowed numeric value. Upper bound of valid range.

schema:stepValue.description: Granularity expected of the value (e.g. 0.1 for nA).

schema:valuePattern.description: Regex pattern for validating string values.

schema:multipleValues.description: Whether multiple values are allowed (default false).

ada:fieldScope.description: Whether this parameter is fixed at the method level, varies per analytical session, or is element-specific.

ada:category.description: Grouping label for form layout (e.g. "Beam Conditions", "Data Processing", "Quality Control"). String for simple cases; DefinedTerm to link to a controlled vocabulary of parameter categories.

ada:dataType.description: Expected data type for the parameter value.

schema:unitCode.description: URI for unit of measure (QUDT preferred).

ada:cdifPropertyPath.description: The CDIF building block property path this parameter maps to. Used for JSON-LD serialisation.

ada:tier.description: Mandatory / Recommended / Optional tier from the metadata profile. Informs validation strictness.

AnalyteColumn.description: Definition of one column in the per-analyte parameter table, typed as schema:PropertyValueSpecification. Each column defines what values are expected per element/oxide row. Analyte rows become schema:variableMeasured entries; columns become schema:additionalProperty within each.

schema:propertyID.description: URI identifying this column's parameter type in a formal vocabulary.

schema:inDefinedTermSet.description:
Controlled vocabulary providing allowed values for this column. Four shapes are accepted: (1) a plain URI string identifying an external SKOS ConceptScheme; (2) an object reference ({"@id": "<uri>"}) to a vocabulary defined elsewhere; (3) a LabeledLink (LinkRole with name and URL); (4) an inline schema:DefinedTermSet enumerating the allowed values
    as schema:DefinedTerm objects (replaces the prior ada:enumeration).

anyOf.description: Object reference to a vocabulary defined elsewhere.
Inline schema:DefinedTermSet listing the allowed values as schema:DefinedTerm objects. Use when no external vocabulary URI is available; replaces the deprecated ada:enumeration property.

schema:defaultValue.description: Default value for this column (pre-filled per row).

schema:readonlyValue.description: true = constant across all analytes (read-only column).

schema:valueRequired.description: true = must be provided for every analyte row.

ada:cdifPropertyPath.description: How this column maps into the variableMeasured JSON-LD structure.

AnalyteIdentifierColumn.description: The mandatory analyte-identifier column. Each row in the analyte table must carry a value for this column naming the analyzed constituent (e.g. "SiO2", "Fe"). Pinned constants enforce the column's role: readonly (the identifier of a row, not an editable parameter), required, mandatory tier, and a fixed mapping into schema:variableMeasured/schema:name. Long-term the value space should be a DefinedTermSet; for now a string.

ComputationalTool.description: Software application used for data acquisition, reduction, or processing. Follows Bioschemas ComputationalTool pattern.

schema:name.description: Name of the software (e.g. "Probe for EPMA").

schema:description.description: Role or purpose of this tool in the method.

schema:url.description: URL to the software product or documentation.

ada:toolRole.description: Role this software plays in the analytical workflow.

Reagent.description: A reference material, calibration standard, or chemical reagent. Follows Bioschemas reagent pattern with extensions for geochemistry reference materials.

schema:name.description: Name of the material (e.g. "San Carlos olivine").

schema:identifier.description: Formal identifier (IGSN, catalog number, GeoReM ID).

ada:reagentRole.description: Role of this material in the method.

schema:citation.description: Publication reference for the standard's accepted values.

ogch.techniqueProtocols.analyteColumns.title: ADA Analyte-Column Specification Registry
ogch.techniqueProtocols.analyteColumns.description: Registry of reusable schema:PropertyValueSpecification analyte-column definitions derived from technique TAPP spreadsheets. Each $def constrains one analyte-table reporting column (e.g. detectionLimit, xrayEmissionLine). TAPP building blocks reference these definitions via fragment $refs (schema.yaml#/$defs/<name>) so they resolve locally through the building-block register. The root only hosts $defs; it has no instantiable properties of its own.

epmaTechnique.title: EPMA Technique per Element
epmaTechnique.description: Whether this element was measured by WDS or EDS.

spectrometerNumber.title: WDS Spectrometer Channel
spectrometerNumber.description: WDS spectrometer number used for this element.

analysisOrder.title: Sequence
analysisOrder.description: Order of analysis on spectormeter. To give an example, if there are 5 detectors, 5 analytes (elements) will be measured simultaneously on the first pass (i.e., Sequence = 1 for all of them), then 5 other analytes will be measured simultaneously on the second pass (i.e., Sequence = 2 for these 5 analytes), etc. The numbering depends on the order of these analytes being measured during an analysis. Also, if there are 20 analytes, there will be at least 4 passes in this case.

monochromatorCrystal.title: Diffracting Crystal
monochromatorCrystal.description: Analysing crystal (monochromator) used in the WDS spectrometer for this element.

wdsDetectorType.title: Proportional Counter / Detector
wdsDetectorType.description: Type of detector used in the WDS spectrometer for this element.

pulseHeightAnalyzeSetting.title: WDS PHA Setting
pulseHeightAnalyzeSetting.description: Pulse height analyzer setting used for the WDS detector.

xrayEmissionLine.title: X-ray Line
xrayEmissionLine.description: The X-ray emission line measured for this element.

peakCountingTime.title: Default Peak Counting Time
peakCountingTime.description: Time spent counting X-ray intensity at the peak position in seconds.

backgroundCountingTime.title: Default Background Counting Time
backgroundCountingTime.description: Total time spent counting at background position(s) in seconds.

backgroundCountingPosition.title: Typical Background Position(s)
backgroundCountingPosition.description: Positions of background measurements relative to the peak, in mm and/or sinθ, and whether on the high or low energy side.

blankCorrection.title: Blank Correction
blankCorrection.description: Method and reference materials used to determine and apply blank corrections.

normalization-standardsCorrection.title: Normalization / Standards-Based Correction
normalization-standardsCorrection.description: Post-acquisition normalization applied using secondary reference materials.

edsDeadTime.title: EDS Dead Time
edsDeadTime.description: Percent dead time reported by the EDS spectrometer

backgroundCorrectionMethod.title: Background Correction Method
backgroundCorrectionMethod.description: Method used to estimate and subtract background X-ray intensity beneath the peak.

timeDependentIntensityCorrection.title: Time-Dependent Intensity Correction
timeDependentIntensityCorrection.description: Type of time-dependent intensity correction applied for volatile or beam-sensitive elements.

elementEstimationMethod.title: Element Estimation Method
elementEstimationMethod.description: How elemental concentrations were calculated — directly from measured X-ray intensities or via cation stoichiometry.

primaryCalibrationStandard.title: Primary Calibration Standard Name
primaryCalibrationStandard.description: Primary reference material used for element standardization (calibration).

secondaryReferenceMaterial.title: Secondary Reference Materials
secondaryReferenceMaterial.description: List of quality-control reference materials (secondary standards) routinely analyzed alongside unknowns.

interferenceCorrection.title: Interference Corrections Applied
interferenceCorrection.description: Flag indicating whether a spectral interference correction was applied for this element.

interferingElements.title: Interfering Elements
interferingElements.description: List of elements whose X-ray lines overlap with the measured line for this element.

interferenceCorrectionStandard.title: Interference Correction Standard
interferenceCorrectionStandard.description: Reference material used to quantify and calibrate the interference correction.

typicalDetectionLimit.title: Typical Detection Limit
typicalDetectionLimit.description: Method detection limit at 99% confidence (3σ) for each measured element.

detectionLimitMethod.title: Detection Limit Method
detectionLimitMethod.description: Method used to compute detection limits.

typicalAnalyticalPrecision.title: Typical Analytical Precision
typicalAnalyticalPrecision.description: Reproducibility of repeated measurements on the same or equivalent standard, expressed as 1σ relative standard deviation (%).

typicalAnalyticalAccuracy.title: Typical Analytical Accuracy
typicalAnalyticalAccuracy.description: Offset between measured and accepted reference values for secondary standards, expressed as % relative bias.

typicalCountingStatisticsError.title: Typical Counting Statistics Error
typicalCountingStatisticsError.description: 1σ uncertainty propagated from counting statistics on peak and background intensities.

spectrometerDwellTime.title: Spectrometer Dwell Time
spectrometerDwellTime.description: Count time (dwell time) per mass position for each measured isotope in milliseconds. Longer dwell times improve counting statistics and lower detection limits but reduce the number of isotopes measurable within a given scan cycle time. For mapping, scan cycle time directly determines spatial resolution at a given scan speed: shorter cycle time = finer spatial resolution.

spotXCoordinate.title: Analysis Location/Spot Coordinates
spotXCoordinate.description: Location of the analysis on the sample surface. For spot and transect analysis: stage coordinates (X, Y in µm) or a description relative to a named reference feature (e.g., mineral rim, inclusion boundary). For mapping: coordinates of the map corner(s) or centre, plus map dimensions. Enables spatial reconstruction and co-registration with other analytical images.

spotYCoordinate.title: Analysis Location/Spot Coordinates
spotYCoordinate.description: Location of the analysis on the sample surface. For spot and transect analysis: stage coordinates (X, Y in µm) or a description relative to a named reference feature (e.g., mineral rim, inclusion boundary). For mapping: coordinates of the map corner(s) or centre, plus map dimensions. Enables spatial reconstruction and co-registration with other analytical images.

spotIdentifier.title: Analysis Location/Spot Coordinates
spotIdentifier.description: Location of the analysis on the sample surface. For spot and transect analysis: stage coordinates (X, Y in µm) or a description relative to a named reference feature (e.g., mineral rim, inclusion boundary). For mapping: coordinates of the map corner(s) or centre, plus map dimensions. Enables spatial reconstruction and co-registration with other analytical images.

IsobaricInterferenceCorrection.title: Isobaric Interference Corrections Applied
IsobaricInterferenceCorrection.description: Whether isobaric interference corrections were applied for any measured isotope in this protocol. A protocol-level Boolean: if the protocol includes interference corrections, this is always Yes. Element-specific detail is captured in Interfering Species and Interference Correction Method.

interferingSpecies.title: Interfering Species
interferingSpecies.description: Elemental or molecular species (oxides, argides, doubly charged ions) overlapping with the measured isotope.

IsobaricInterferenceCorrectionMethod.title: Interference Correction Method
IsobaricInterferenceCorrectionMethod.description: Equation or procedure used to correct for isobaric interferences, including the production rate factor and the reference material used to measure it.

detectionLimit.title: Detection Limit
detectionLimit.description: Session detection limit for each measured isotope, expressed in µg g⁻¹, ng g⁻¹, or wt% as appropriate. Report the value(s) and units per isotope or element group. Mandatory at analysis level to demonstrate the reliability of reported near-detection-limit concentrations. The calculation method is captured separately in Detection Limit Method.

limitOfQuantification.title: Limit of Quantification (LOQ) Method
limitOfQuantification.description: Reference or description of the method used to calculate the limit of quantification (LOQ): the lowest concentration reliably measurable with acceptable precision and accuracy. Mandatory at analysis level when concentrations near the LOD are reported. Concentrations between LOD and LOQ are detectable but not reliably quantifiable.

withinSessionReproducibility.title: Within-Session Analytical Precision and Assessment Method
withinSessionReproducibility.description: Reproducibility of repeated measurements within a single analytical session. Report both the assessment method and the precision values. Assessment method must specify: (1) the reference material used, (2) number of replicates n, and (3) the statistic reported (1σ RSD, 2σ RSD, etc.). For mapping: assess from repeated analyses of a reference material area at session start and end, or from replicate analyses of a homogeneous reference phase within the map.

enum: Within-Session Analytical Precision and Assessment Method

withinSessionReproducibilityMethod.title: Within-Session Analytical Precision and Assessment Method
withinSessionReproducibilityMethod.description: Reproducibility of repeated measurements within a single analytical session. Report both the assessment method and the precision values. Assessment method must specify: (1) the reference material used, (2) number of replicates n, and (3) the statistic reported (1σ RSD, 2σ RSD, etc.). For mapping: assess from repeated analyses of a reference material area at session start and end, or from replicate analyses of a homogeneous reference phase within the map.

enum: Within-Session Analytical Precision and Assessment Method

betweenSessionReproducibility.title: Between-Session (Long-Term) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method
betweenSessionReproducibility.description: Reproducibility of measurements across multiple analytical sessions over weeks to months (long-term or intermediate precision). Report both the assessment method and the precision values. Specify: reference material used, number of sessions n, time span covered, and statistic reported. Long-term precision is typically assessed from a compiled record of secondary reference material values across all sessions.

enum: Between-Session (Long-Term) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method

betweenSessionReproducibilityMethod.title: Between-Session (Long-Term) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method
betweenSessionReproducibilityMethod.description: Reproducibility of measurements across multiple analytical sessions over weeks to months (long-term or intermediate precision). Report both the assessment method and the precision values. Specify: reference material used, number of sessions n, time span covered, and statistic reported. Long-term precision is typically assessed from a compiled record of secondary reference material values across all sessions.

enum: Between-Session (Long-Term) Analytical Precision and Assessment Method

analyticalAccuracy.title: Analytical Accuracy and Assessment Method
analyticalAccuracy.description: Offset between measured and accepted reference values for secondary reference materials, expressed as % relative bias. Report both the assessment method and the accuracy values. Specify: (1) secondary RM used and source of reference values, (2) number of analyses, and (3) elements or element groups assessed. Report any systematic biases and likely causes.

analyticalAccuracyMethod.title: Analytical Accuracy and Assessment Method
analyticalAccuracyMethod.description: Offset between measured and accepted reference values for secondary reference materials, expressed as % relative bias. Report both the assessment method and the accuracy values. Specify: (1) secondary RM used and source of reference values, (2) number of analyses, and (3) elements or element groups assessed. Report any systematic biases and likely causes.

ogch.techniqueProtocols.parameterTemplat.title: ADA Method-Parameter Template Registry
ogch.techniqueProtocols.parameterTemplat.description: Registry of reusable schema:PropertyValueSpecification method-parameter templates derived from technique TAPP spreadsheets. Each $def constrains one method-level (readOnly:true) parameter template (e.g. DriftCorrection, massAbsorptionCoefficients). TAPP building blocks reference these definitions via fragment $refs (schema.yaml#/$defs/<name>) so they resolve locally through the building-block register. The root only hosts $defs; it has no instantiable properties of its own.

BeamDamageMinimization.title: Beam Damage Minimization
BeamDamageMinimization.description: Description of the approach used to minimize beam damage, especially Na- and K-loss in glasses, micas, and hydrous minerals.

DriftCorrection.title: Drift Correction
DriftCorrection.description: Describe method used to monitor and correct for instrument drift

massAbsorptionCoefficients.title: Mass Absorption Coefficients (MACs)
massAbsorptionCoefficients.description: Database of mass absorption coefficients used in the matrix correction.

halogenOxygenCorrection.title: Halogen Correction on Oxygen
halogenOxygenCorrection.description: Whether a halogen correction was applied to calculate oxygen content by stoichiometry in halogen-bearing phases.

wdsDeadTimeCorrection.title: WDS Dead Time Correction
wdsDeadTimeCorrection.description: Method used to correct WDS proportional counter dead time at high count rates.

edsSpectralProcessingType.title: EDS Spectral Processing Type
edsSpectralProcessingType.description: Method used to process EDS spectra and extract net peak intensities.

LaserPulseDuration.title: Laser Pulse Duration
LaserPulseDuration.description: Duration of each individual laser pulse, including units. Pulse duration determines the ablation regime: nanosecond (ns) pulses involve significant thermal effects and elemental fractionation; femtosecond (fs) pulses are non-thermal and substantially reduce elemental fractionation and matrix effects. This is a fixed hardware property of the laser system.

WarmUpTime.title: Instrument Warm-up / Session Duration Limit
WarmUpTime.description: Minimum warm-up time required after plasma ignition before analyses begin, and any maximum session duration enforced to maintain stable operating conditions. These constraints are part of the protocol and cannot be varied by the analyst.

SessionDurationLimit.title: Instrument Warm-up / Session Duration Limit
SessionDurationLimit.description: Minimum warm-up time required after plasma ignition before analyses begin, and any maximum session duration enforced to maintain stable operating conditions. These constraints are part of the protocol and cannot be varied by the analyst.

DriftMonitorFrequency.title: Multi-Run Sequential Analysis Design
DriftMonitorFrequency.description: Whether the protocol uses a single acquisition pass or multiple sequential runs on the same sample location, each optimized for different analytical objectives. For multi-run designs, describe the number of runs, their purpose, key laser and instrument settings per run, and how outputs of one run feed into data reduction of another. Not applicable to raster mapping, where each spatial location is visited exactly once.

MatrixOffseCorrection.title: Matrix Offset Correction (LIEF)
MatrixOffseCorrection.description: Whether an empirical correction was applied to account for systematic differences in laser-induced elemental fractionation (LIEF) patterns between the external calibration standard and the sample matrix.

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.id.description:
Properties for a schema.org identifier (schema:PropertyValue pattern).

**Union-type policy:** In CDIF profile UML models an attribute typed as
schema:Identifier / schema:PropertyValue is represented by a single attribute
of that class type. The JSON Schema implementation permits the property value
to be EITHER a plain string (interpreted as the bare identifier value) OR a
full schema:PropertyValue object (with explicit @type, propertyID, value).
Consumers should accept either form.

schema:propertyID.description: In this context for the schema:PropertyValue, this field is an identifier for the identifier schema, e.g. DOI, ARK.  Get values from https://registry.identifiers.org/registry/ for interoperability

schema:url.description: web-resolveable string for the identifier; host name part is location of a resolver that will return some representation for the given identifier value. E.g. https://doi.org/10.5066/F7VX0DMQ

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.de.description:
schema.org Defined Term schema.

**Union-type policy:** In CDIF profile UML models an attribute typed as
schema:DefinedTerm is represented by a single attribute of that class type.
The JSON Schema implementation permits the property value to be EITHER a
plain string (interpreted as schema:name or schema:termCode in the default
vocabulary) OR a full schema:DefinedTerm object (with explicit @type, name,
identifier, termCode, inDefinedTermSet). Consumers should accept either form.

Note that this differs from the cdif Concept policy: a Concept (skos:Concept)
in CDIF profiles MUST be a controlled-vocabulary entry (object form or
@id-reference) — plain strings are not permitted for Concept-typed values
because vocabulary identity cannot be recovered from an unscoped label.

schema:name.description: text label for the term that is useful to human user

schema:inDefinedTermSet.description: Name for the controlled vocabulary responsible for this keyword.

schema:termCode.description: A representative code for this keyword in the controlled vocabulary. Analogous to skos:Notation

ogch.geochemProperties.instrument.title: ADA Analysis Instrument
ogch.geochemProperties.instrument.description: ADA analytical instrument building block. Extends the core CDIF instrument building block with NeXus NXinstrument classification via additionalType. Instruments are typed as schema:Thing + schema:Product (from core) with domain-specific types (e.g. nxs:BaseClass/NXinstrument, ada:AMSInstrument) in additionalType.

schema:additionalType.description: Domain-specific instrument type classifications. Should include a NeXus base class (e.g. nxs:BaseClass/NXinstrument) and/or technique-specific identifier (e.g. ada:AMSInstrument, GCMD instrument identifier).

ogch.geochemProperties.laboratory.title: ADA Analysis Laboratory
ogch.geochemProperties.laboratory.description: ADA laboratory or facility building block. Extends the core CDIF spatialExtent (schema:Place) with NeXus NXsource classification via additionalType. Inherits place name, identifier, alternateName, geo coordinates, and geosparql geometry from spatialExtent.

schema:additionalType.description: Must include nxs:BaseClass/NXsource for NeXus facility classification.

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.pe.description: schema for cdif profile of schema.org/Person

schema:name.description: string label for person that is meaningful for human users, should format consistently. Recommend 'Family Name, Given name' format.

schema:alternateName.description: other labels by which the person might be known

schema:affiliation.description: if affiliation is present, value must be a schema:Organization.

schema:contactPoint.description: restrict to email only. Schema.org allows telephone and postal contacts as well

schema:name.description: string label for organization that is meaningful for human users

schema:alternateName.description: other labels by which the organization might be known

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.la.description: schema for a labeled link, a profile of schema.org/CreativeWork

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.mo.description: Funding acknowledgement properties, profile of schema.org/MonetaryGrant

@id.description: URI identifier for this funding record

schema:description.description: description of the funding or grant

@id.description: a identifier for an agent defined in this metadata, or externally; must be dereferenceable

cdif.bbr.metadata.qualityProperties.qual.title: definitions for simple quality measure property

dqv:isMeasurementOf.description: specify the quality measure that is reported, by name, with an ID ref, or as a Defined Term

@id.description: a resolvable reference to a representation of a quality measure

dqv:value.description: the reported result of the quality measure, either as a string or a defined term from a vocabulary

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.in.title: Instrument Description
cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.in.description: Schema for describing laboratory instruments and instrument systems. Supports ownership, manufacturer, model, commissioning dates, hierarchical sub-components via schema:hasPart, and domain-specific typing. Instruments may be standalone devices or complex systems with sub-components.

@id.description: Persistent identifier URI for this instrument metadata record.

@type.description: Must include schema:Product and schema:Thing. May include additional types.

schema:additionalType.description: Domain-specific type classifications. Should include a scientific instrument type URI (e.g. wd:Q3099911 for Wikidata scientific instrument).

schema:description.description: Text description of this instrument, its purpose, and capabilities.

schema:alternateName.description: Alternate name(s), e.g. specific make/model designation, common abbreviation.

schema:identifier.description: Formal identifier(s) for this instrument. Use PropertyValue for structured identifiers (e.g. PIDINST, serial number, inventory number).

schema:url.description: Landing page URL for this instrument.

schema:model.description: Product model information for this instrument.

schema:category.description: Instrument type classification(s) from a controlled vocabulary.

schema:contributor.description: Agents associated with this instrument in specific roles (e.g. operator, custodian, principal investigator). Use schema:owner for the owning organization.

schema:additionalProperty.description: Instrument-specific properties (measured variables, detection limits, calibration information, operating parameters, etc.).

schema:validThrough.description: Date the instrument was decommissioned (ISO 8601). Absent if still operational.

schema:hasPart.description: Sub-components of this instrument system. Each item is either an inline instrument description or an @id reference.

@id.description: Reference to a sub-component defined elsewhere.

schema:relatedLink.description: Links to related resources (manuals, datasheets, calibration records, related instruments).

schema:subjectOf.description: Catalog record metadata-about-metadata for this instrument description.

schema:dateModified.description: Date this metadata record was last modified (ISO 8601).

dcterms:conformsTo.description: Schema or profile this metadata record conforms to.

InstrumentComponent.description: A sub-component of an instrument system. Uses the same structure as the parent instrument but without nesting (single level of hasPart).

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.sp.description: Spatial Extent description for CDIF discovery profile.  Note required prefix declaration for geoSparql ( http://www.opengis.net/ont/geosparql#) and OGC simple features (sf: http://www.opengis.net/ont/sf#)

schema:additionalType.description: Domain-specific type classifications for this place (e.g. facility type,laboratory classification, feature type).

schema:name.description: A place name for the location, either as a string or a DefinedTerm from a gazetteer.

schema:identifier.description: Formal identifier for this place (e.g. ROR identifier for a facility).

schema:alternateName.description: Alternate or abbreviated name(s) for this place.

schema:geo.description: Either a bounding box or a point location.

anyOf.description: A point location. Point locations are recommended for data that is associated with specific sample locations, particularly if these are widely spaced such that an enclosing bounding box would be a misleading representation of the spatial location. Be aware that some client applications might only index or display bounding box extents or a single point location.

A schema:GeoShape bounding box. The geometry is described with a set of latitude/longitude pairs (in that order).The documentation for schema:GeoShape states 'Either whitespace or commas can be used to separate latitude and longitude; whitespace should be used when writing a list of several such points.'

schema:box.description: A GeoShape box defines an area on the surface of the earth defined by point locations of the southwest corner and northeast corner of the rectangle in latitude-longitude coordinates. A space should be used to separate the latitude and longitude values. The two corner coordinate points are separated by a space. 'East longitude' means positive longitude values are east of the prime (Greenwich) meridian.

anyOf.description: A schema:GeoShape curvilinear trace, for resource related to a linear trace like a ship track or airplane flight line

schema:line.description: A GeoShape box defines a curvilinear geometry as a string of latitude-longitude coordinates. A space should be used to separate the latitude and longitude values. The coordinate point pairs are also separated by a space. 'East longitude' means positive longitude values are east of the prime (Greenwich) meridian. e.g. '39.33 120.77 40.44 123.96 41.00 121.34'

geosparql:hasGeometry.description: Optional geographic extent using wkt geometry, see Ocean InfoHub (https://book.oceaninfohub.org/thematics/spatial/README.html#simple-geosparql-wkt). Other geometry schemes might be specified in a specific domain profile, e.g. for atmospheric, subsurface data, or local coordinate systems. NOTE that the location specified here should be the same as the schema.org point or contained within the specified bounding box.

@type.description: MUST be sf: (<http://www.opengis.net/ont/sf#>) SimpleFeature geometry type. See https://opengeospatial.github.io/ogc-geosparql/geosparql11/sf_geometries.ttl

@value.description: a WKT geometry description string, e.g. 'POINT(-76 -18)'

@id.description: identifier string for coordinate reference system, e.g., 'CRS84'

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.ag.description: For more granularity on how a person contributed to a Dataset, use schema:Role. The schema.org documentation does not state that the Role type is an expected data type of author, creator and contributor, but that is addressed in this blog post (http://blog.schema.org/2014/06/introducing-role.html). see https://github.com/ESIPFed/science-on-schema.org/blob/develop/guides/Dataset.md#roles-of-people

@id.description: IRI reference to a Person or Organization defined elsewhere

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.ad.title: additionalProperty PropertyValue
cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.ad.description: PropertyValue values required to define a soft-typed property with a value.

schema:propertyID.description: identifier or name for the property concept quantified by the values in this variable slot. Multiple values can specify the property at different levels of granularity.

cdif.bbr.metadata.cdifProperties.cdifRef.description: Building block to implement relations to other resources using a URL and some semantics.

Relation.description: DCAT Relationship surface added on top of the schema.org labeled link construct.

dcat:hadRole.description: Role of the related resource as a SKOS Concept (DCAT canonical role slot).

dcterms:relation.description: URI of the related resource (DCAT canonical pointer to what is being related to; distinct from schema:url which is the presentation URL inherited from labeledLink).

cdif.bbr.metadata.skosProperties.skosCon.title: SKOS Concept
cdif.bbr.metadata.skosProperties.skosCon.description: JSON Schema for a SKOS Concept in JSON-LD form. A unit of thought within a concept scheme. Supports labels (prefLabel, altLabel, hiddenLabel), notations, hierarchical relations (broader/narrower), associative relations (related), cross-scheme mapping properties, scheme membership, and documentary notes. Based on the W3C SKOS Reference (https://www.w3.org/TR/skos-reference/).

@context.description: JSON-LD context declaring the skos namespace prefix. May be a single object or an array of strings and objects.

skos:prefLabel.description: Preferred lexical label for this concept. A single string, a single language-tagged value, or an array of language-tagged values. Each language should appear at most once.

skos:hiddenLabel.description: Labels accessible to free-text search but not displayed.

skos:notation.description: Classification code for this concept within a scheme.

skos:definition.description: Formal explanation of the meaning of this concept.

skos:scopeNote.description: Note clarifying meaning and/or intended use.

skos:historyNote.description: Note about past state or use.

skos:example.description: Example of use of this concept.

skos:inScheme.description: Concept scheme(s) this concept belongs to.

skos:topConceptOf.description: Concept scheme(s) for which this is a top concept.

skos:broader.description: Broader (parent) concepts in the hierarchy. Items are inline concept objects or @id references.

skos:narrower.description: Narrower (child) concepts in the hierarchy. Items are inline concept objects or @id references.

skos:exactMatch.description: Concepts in other schemes with equivalent meaning.

skos:closeMatch.description: Concepts in other schemes with similar meaning.

ConceptRef.description: A reference to a SKOS Concept by URI.

LanguageTaggedValue.description: An RDF literal value with a language tag, serialized as a JSON-LD value object.

@language.description: BCP 47 language tag (e.g. en, fr, de).

title: EMPA Technique-Aligned Protocol Profile (empaTAPP)
description: EMPA-specific extension of the base TAPP definition. Adds top-level EPMA properties (beam mode, accelerating voltage default, matrix correction method, etc.), a parameter vocabulary in ada:methodParameters, and an analyte-column template covering EPMA per-element acquisition and reporting fields. Each ada:analyteColumns[] entry must match one of the catalog files in analyteColumns/ (or the inherited identifier column from tappDefinition); each catalog file is itself a JSON Schema whose examples[0] carries the canonical instance. Generated from docs/TAPP_EPMA_filled.xlsx by tools/build_empaTAPP_from_spreadsheet.py.

ada:beamMode.description: Whether the beam was focused, defocused, or rastered over an area.

ada:acceleratingVoltageDefault.description: Electron beam accelerating voltage in kilovolts (kV).

ada:beamDiameterDefault.description: Diameter of the focused or defocused electron beam in micrometers.

ada:matrixCorrectionMethod.description: X-ray matrix correction algorithm applied during data reduction.

schema:hasPart.description: Instrument sub-components. Each item is a schema:Thing with at least one schema:additionalType. Spreadsheet-known types: ElectronSource, edsDetector, wdsSpectrometer. Other additionalType values are accepted via the catch-all branch.

oneOf.description: Catch-all for instrument sub-component types not enumerated above. Authors may use any schema:additionalType outside the known set; schema:name is unconstrained on this branch.
